financing.summary: Private, 100% ESOP-owned builder with no public debt, ratings or financial statements, so almost all of its capital structure is not publicly disclosed. What county records (as reported by Talk Business) show is a three-part land model in Northwest Arkansas: land banking of finished lots with TPG Angelo Gordon's Essential Housing (three recorded two-year option deals from Dec 2025 to Oct 2026 covering 248 lots and about $22.2M), finished lots bought or contracted from third-party developers (Calara, Kinney Creek, Three Pistols, Saddle Hill Estates), and raw land or lot purchases funded with short local bank loans (First National Bank of Fort Smith, North American Savings Bank, earlier City Bank of Lubbock). It also moves small batches of completed homes into a wholly owned rental affiliate, Steppingstone Home Rentals LLC, financed by Arvest Bank. A competitor is already the incumbent land banker, but only Northwest Arkansas deals are visible; Springfield, Joplin and the new Tulsa market show no public land-bank activity, which is where room for a second provider is most plausible.
financing.land_strategy: Mixed and shifting land-lighter. In 2020 the company was described as self-developing most of its lots (buying raw land, entitling it and installing infrastructure), for example the 400-lot Orchard Park subdivision in Centerton. Since late 2025 it has added finished-lot option agreements with Essential Housing and a developer partnership with Calara, while still buying raw land outright (62.85 acres in Gravette, Oct 2026). No stated owned/optioned target.

lots.note: Lot counts are not publicly disclosed (private company). Only deal-level counts are public: 248 lots under Essential Housing option agreements and 154 lots contracted from Calara in Northwest Arkansas.

land_banking.description: Program-level announcement: a strategic land-financing partnership under which Essential Housing finances finished lots across multiple developments and markets for the builder, with Whelan Advisory as the builder's exclusive financial advisor. Size not disclosed.

land_banking.note: Seen in search snippet, not confirmed: the Builder article returned 403 and could not be opened, and no press release was found on another site. Date not visible; the snippet cites the builder's 2025 Builder 100 rank, so it ran between mid-2025 and spring 2026. The three recorded deals above corroborate the relationship.

land_banking.description: Land development partnership in Rogers, AR: Calara took assignment of the builder's land contract, bought the site for $3.17M, will develop about 154 large single-family lots and has the finished lots contracted for sale to Schuber Mitchell Homes. Start is tied to a City of Rogers sewer upgrade.

capital_events.description: Bought 162 acres of subdivision-ready land in Centerton, AR for $3.4M, financed by City Bank of Lubbock, Texas (loan amount not stated).
capital_events.source_title: Talk Business & Politics: Real Deals: Schuber Mitchell pays $3.4 million for Centerton land

capital_events.description: The three shareholders (Daman Schuber, Dan Mitchell and Joe Harris) sold 100% of the stock to a newly created employee stock ownership plan; the company had reorganised as a Public Benefit Corporation in February 2020. Atlantic Management Company advised the ESOP trustee.
capital_events.source_title: Atlantic Management Company advises on ESOP transaction for Schuber Mitchell Homes (press release)
capital_events.note: Price, seller notes and any ESOP acquisition debt are not disclosed. An ESOP-owned builder cannot easily raise outside equity, which makes off-balance-sheet lot financing more useful to it.
